overview: Pragmatic trial with individual allocation on the postnatal ward, over 18 months, comparing remote blood pressure monitoring with midwife hub titration against usual community checks for women discharged after a hypertensive disorder of pregnancy.
population: Women aged 16 and over discharged after pre-eclampsia or gestational hypertension who consent before discharge; women without a smartphone or needing an interpreter are included with a loan phone, a paper diary with hub calls, or interpreter calls.
exposure: A validated upper-arm monitor with a cuff sized at discharge; readings twice daily for two weeks, then daily to six weeks, sent by app, text or phone; hub midwives adjust medicines under protocol MAT-HTN-04 and call after high readings; out-of-hours severe readings go to the maternity assessment unit.
procedures: Allocation by a central web service after consent on the postnatal ward, stratified by pre-eclampsia versus gestational hypertension. Usual care continues in both arms. The six-week blood pressure is taken at the family doctor visit and retrieved from the shared record; readmissions from hospital records.

outcomes.name: Blood pressure control at six weeks
outcomes.measure: Blood pressure below 140 over 90 at the six-week check, from the shared record
outcomes.why: Measurable in both arms from routine care and linked to long-term cardiovascular risk; readmission is too rare to power.

outcomes.name: Readmission or unplanned attendance for hypertension
outcomes.measure: Hospital readmission or assessment unit attendance for hypertension within six weeks
outcomes.why: The outcome women care most about; reported with its interval.

outcomes.name: Severe readings treated within 24 hours
outcomes.measure: Proportion of readings of 160 over 110 or more followed by treatment within 24 hours (remote arm) or recorded severe hypertension events (both arms)
outcomes.why: Severe peaks are the danger remote monitoring aims to catch.

outcomes.name: Uptake and reporting by digital access and language
outcomes.measure: Proportion reporting readings on at least 10 of the first 14 days, by smartphone ownership and interpreter need

outcomes.name: Burden and low blood pressure
outcomes.measure: Two-item burden question at six weeks; symptomatic low blood pressure after titration
outcomes.why: Monitoring should not overload new mothers or over-treat.

feasibility: About 412 eligible women a year; with about 55 percent consenting, about 340 women in 18 months, within the 300 funded monitors for the remote arm.
biasMitigation: Primary outcome from routine six-week measurement in both arms
Intention-to-treat analysis including women who never report

biasFlags.label: Missing six-week readings
biasFlags.note: Family doctor checks may be missed more in one arm; retrieval from the shared record and a reminder in both arms.

biasFlags.label: Contamination through midwives
biasFlags.note: Community midwives may adjust care for usual-care women; accepted as pragmatic.

biasFlags.label: Selective consent
biasFlags.note: Consent rates by language and digital access are reported.

flags: Stratification by diagnosis is the only adjustment
parsimony.simplestPath: Individual allocation, one routine primary outcome, two secondary outcomes, inclusive delivery.

theoreticalFramework: None beyond describing the intervention with TIDieR.
summary: Pragmatic trial with six-week control as the primary outcome, readmission and severe readings as secondary, and inclusion measured as a process outcome.
